screenings.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
screenings.description: Harry is an old-school hustler. A classic native New Yorker, he moves through life lubricating palms with cash, relying on his wits and connections. But times are changing for Harry. His daily pickpocket take isn’t green bills and wristwatches, it’s credit cards and cell phones. And one unfortunate night, cryptocurrency and a handgun. THE ONLY LIVING PICKPOCKET IN NEW YORK is a nostalgic portrait of a small-time career criminal navigating today's digitally networked world. Writer/Director Noah Segan's modern metropolis is powered by the ephemera of a time gone by, with shoe-leather action brought to radiant life by a terrific cast, led by John Turturro's exceptional turn as Harry.

screenings.title: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth

screenings.title: Suspiria [4K DCP]
screenings.description: A fairy tale construction at once grim and florid, Argento’s best-known film finds Jessica Harper’s American ballet dancer arriving at an exclusive academy in Germany where she discovers a dark past and occult forces at work in the present. With some of Argento’s most perversely ingenious set pieces, a plum part for former Fritz Lang muse Joan Bennett, and a spine-tingling theme by Goblin that will haunt you to the grave.

screenings.title: Earth Girls Are Easy
screenings.description: In this musical comedy, Valerie is dealing with her philandering fiancé, Ted, when she finds that a trio of aliens have crashed their spaceship into her swimming pool. Once the furry beings are shaved at her girlfriend’s salon, the women discover three handsome men underneath. After absorbing the native culture via television, the spacemen are ready to hit the dating scene in 1980s Los Angeles.

screenings.title: The Holy Mountain
screenings.description: The follow-up to his Midnight Movie sensation El Topo, writer-director Alejandro Jodorowsky’s THE HOLY MOUNTAIN caused a scandal at the 1973 Cannes Film Festival with its flood of sacrilegious imagery, existential symbolism and outrageous violence. Once again, Jodorowsky plays the allegorically named lead, “The Alchemist,” who assembles a group of people from all walks of life and renames them for the planets in the solar system. Putting his recruits through strange mystical rites and divesting them of their worldly baggage, he leads them on a trip to Lotus Island to ascend the Holy Mountain and displace the immortal gods who secretly rule the universe. This gorgeous new digital restoration, overseen by the filmmaker himself, returns Jodorowsky’s most visually extravagant film to all its trippy splendor.

screenings.title: The Devils
screenings.description: Assembled from the original camera negative, this new 4K restoration presents Ken Russell’s definitive vision of The Devils by referencing the edit he privately constructed in 2004. The film’s sound has been remastered from original English Composite 35mm Mag Film, transferred at 96kHz, plus other original film elements in selected spots as needed. The Picture and Sound restoration was performed by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color, and Warner Bros. Sound.

screenings.title: The Conversation
screenings.description: Coppola’s masterful thriller and Cannes Palme d’Or winner showcases what may be Gene Hackman’s greatest performance. Lonely wiretapping expert and devout Catholic Harry Caul (Hackman) is hired to record a seemingly innocuous conversation between two lovers in San Francisco’s Union Square. Upon re-hearing the tapes, however, Caul believes he may be putting the couple in danger if he turns the material over to his client (Robert Duvall). But what one hears can ultimately turn out to be quite different from what was actually recorded.

screenings.title: Young Blondes Stalked and Murdered
screenings.description: On the occasion of the upcoming release of his new film THE HEDONIST (2025), Spectacle presents Nick Funess’ rarely-screened debut feature YOUNG BLONDES, STALKED AND MURDERED (2024). The title says it all. After young actresses start mysteriously going missing, struggling actress Stacy (Samantha Carroll) begins to believe that she is being followed by a serial killer. In a shallow environment where all attention is good attention, that may not be such a bad thing.

screenings.title: Female Trouble
screenings.description: “Sex offenses that would shock the Marquis de Sade!” sniffed critic Rex Reed in the Daily News, reviewing John Waters’ follow-up to the notorious Pink Flamingos. The perversities pile up in the tale of high-school delinquent and meatball sandwich-lover Dawn Davenport (played by Waters muse Divine), whose number one Christmas wish is for a pair of cha-cha heels. But her parents fail to heed her request, and her rage leads inexorably to stripping, prostitution, disfigurement, tabloid fame and mass murder.

As the threat of violence escalates, Irwin’s wife Hester (Scarlett Johansson) sounds the alarm, Irwin desperately tries to protect his family, and Gary is forced to make an impossible choice to save those he loves.

screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.title: Ben'imana
screenings.description: In 2012, eighteen years after the genocide against the Tutsi, a Rwandan village is still learning how to live with itself. Vénéranda has spent years helping survivors and the families of those responsible speak the words that were never said between them. However, forgiveness comes easier when it’s someone else’s story. When her own daughter’s future becomes entangled with the past, Vénéranda is forced to find her own words at last.

screenings.description: Raanan, a middle aged man, returns home after 30 years abroad. A chance encounter with an elderly man unlocks troubled memories, and a brief affair with a much younger man, send him spiraling through generational rifts, and force him to confront his internalized homophobia and emotional wounds of his past.

screenings.title: 14th
screenings.description: Written in the wreckage of the Civil War, the 14th Amendment was meant to codify the promise of freedom and citizenship. Instead, it has become a permanent argument. Oscar nominee DuVernay’s new documentary pulls this fight out of the footnotes and into the present, chronicling a vicious battle that has raged for more than 150 years. Threading deep archival scholarship with today’s headlines, 14TH brings together legal minds, politicians, historians and cultural voices to explore a question America still hasn’t settled: Who gets to belong?

screenings.title: The Rescuers
screenings.description: Geraldine Page, Bob Newhart, and Eva Gabor are among the vocal talent assembled for Disney’s vivacious adaptation of Margery Sharp’s beloved book series about the Rescue Aid Society, a group of dauntless mice who travel the world to lend aid to kidnapping victims. Here R.A.S. representatives Miss Bianca (Gabor) and Bernard (Newhart) rush to Devil’s Bayou, Louisiana, where they liberate a little girl named Penny from the clutches of the nefarious Madame Medusa (Page) and her trained crocodiles, Brutus and Nero, while at the same time tasked with keeping a precious gemstone safe from the villainess. A spirited, swashbuckling adventure, made with brio by Disney’s crack animation team led by rising star Don Bluth.

screenings.title: The Ascent
screenings.description: The bloodthirsty and seemingly unstoppable Nazi war machine is on the march towards Moscow in Shepitko’s wrenching, snow-swept World War II drama, which begins with two Soviet peasant soldiers foraging for food in a Belarusian village and proceeds to tell an emotional, lyrical tale of loyalty and betrayal, partisanship and collaboration, and, ultimately, the possibility of transcendent redemption. Shepitko’s final feature, frequently cited as among the greatest of Soviet films, won the Golden Bear at the 1977 Berlin Film Festival, just two years before its director’s tragic death in a car accident at age 41.

screenings.description: Thirty-four days before she’s sent to prison, notorious Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a skeptical film crew to document her every move. What begins as an intimate portrait of an enigmatic felon becomes a mind-bending three-year journey into the abyss.

screenings.title: A Boy Named Charlie Brown
screenings.description: Dir. Bill Melendez. 1969, 85 mins. U.S. 35mm. The beautifully animated A Boy Named Charlie Brown was the first theatrical Peanuts feature, and it remains the best. Directed by Disney and Looney Tunes animation veteran Bill Melendez, whom cartoonist Charles M. Schulz had first entrusted with bringing his characters to life on the groundbreaking television specials A Charlie Brown Christmas and It’s the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown, this gentle musical comedy follows our eternally disappointed “blockhead” as he navigates baseball losses, kite-eating trees, and his own anxieties while preparing to compete in the National Spelling Bee championship in New York. Linus and Lucy, Schroeder and Snoopy—the whole gang—is here, as is the great Vince Guaraldi, supplying a jazzy, Oscar-nominated score, plus a musical centerpiece dream sequence set to Beethoven’s Sonata Pathétique, which expands the animated world of the Peanuts into uncharted realms of visual experimentation. Tickets: $17.50 / $12 senior and students / $10 youth / free for MoMI members. There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership. Order tickets. Please pick up tickets at the Museum’s admissions desk upon arrival. All seating is general admission.

screenings.description: ASH AND CRAYONS, a documentary by Academy Award®-nominated director Evgeny Afineevsky, is an intimate portrait of childhood resilience and hope amid the war in Ukraine. The film follows seven children as they pursue their passions, support their families, build friendships, and continue moving forward with courage and determination. While rooted in the experiences of Ukrainian children, the film speaks to a universal truth: that even in the face of devastation, the human spirit has an extraordinary capacity to endure, adapt, and dream of a better tomorrow.

screenings.title: In Waves
screenings.description: Amid the sun-filled surf culture of SoCal, two lovestruck teens face a tragic twist of fate but find strength in friends and the ocean. In French and English with English subtitles.

screenings.title: Digger
screenings.description: The most powerful man in the world races to prove he is humanity’s savior before the disaster he unleashed destroys everything.

screenings.title: All of a Sudden
screenings.description: Japan’s Official Selection for Best International Feature Film at the 99th Academy Awards® WINNER, BEST ACTRESS (VIRGINIE EFIRA & TAO OKAMOTO), 2026 CANNES FILM FESTIVAL In the latest film by Oscar®-winning director Ryûsuke Hamaguchi (DRIVE MY CAR), Virginie Efira (BENEDETTA) stars as Marie-Lou, the progressive director of a nursing home in the Parisian suburbs. Her life changes when she meets Mari (Tao Okamoto), Japanese playwright. As the two women reckon with the lives they have lived, they find new ways to make sense of the time that remains. Following caregivers as they navigate the tensions between idealism and pragmatism, Hamaguchi crafts a film that rests fully in the present, attentive to the delicate unfolding of thought, feeling, and human connection. Presented with support from The Reginald S. Reinhardt, Ling-Makekau Fund for Asia-Pacific Films 2026 196 MIN. FRANCE / JAPAN / GERMANY / BELGIUM IN ENGLISH, FRENCH, AND JAPANESE WITH ENGLISH SUBTITLES NEON Open Caption (OC) Screenings: Wednesday, November 25, 12:15 show Thursday, November 26, 12:15 show Saturday, November 28, 12:15 show Sunday, November 29, 12:15 show Monday, November 30, 12:15 show Thursday, December 3, 6:30 show

screenings.title: Voyage to Italy
screenings.description: VIAGGIO IN ITALIA Italy/France, 1954 Directed by Roberto Rossellini Starring Ingrid Bergman, George Sanders, Maria Mauban In Italian with English subtitles. Approx. 97 min. New 4K restoration. In Naples to sell a late uncle’s villa, London business man George Sanders and wife Ingrid Bergman find that, after eight years of marriage, they have little to say to each other. And as the closing drags on, Bergman remembers a died-too-young poet who loved her, Sanders frets about time away from work, and they split apart—she to stare at the rawness of the statuary in the Museum, the ionization of Vesuvian craters, the skeletons at the cemetery; he to dally with friends on Capri, languidly pursue an estranged wife, and to wave off an attractive prostitute; both to finally view the plaster molds of the dead of Pompeii. Little happens, and yet subtly we see the degeneration of a marriage. Will it take a miracle to save it? Unsuccessful on first release, but over the years steadily climbing the ranks of All-Time Ten Best lists. New 4K restoration from Cinecittà. Presented with support from The Ada Katz Fund for Literature in Film

screenings.title: Fatherland
screenings.description: ★★★★★ “Another expansive, enriching work from a modern master.” – Phil de Semlyen, Time Out “A perfectly cut jewel of a movie... The power of the movie creeps up on you with its emotional restraint, the beauty of its black-and-white images and the delicacy with which Pawlikowski explores the devastations trembling under the faces of both father and daughter...” – Manohla Dargis, The New York Times “Stunning... an exquisite study of family, identity, and art where future ideals are intertwined with historical remorse.” – Tomris Laffly, Elle “[A] damn-near perfect period piece... Told with exacting restraint yet as layered as the lacquer on an ebony Biedermeier console, this forms a loose triptych with Pawlikowski’s last two features, IDA and COLD WAR, both of which were set at least partly behind the Iron Curtain... It is immaculately performed by Zischler and especially Hüller, grounding the film throughout with an uncanny, expressive stillness. But it is also exquisitely rendered in the same boxy ratio and silvery monochrome lensing Pawlikowski and DP Lukasz Zal (THE ZONE OF INTEREST) deployed on IDA and COLD WAR, and scrupulously detailed down to the ruined buildings, sharply cut suits, surly restaurant service and eclectic selection of jazz, classical and folk tunes chosen by Pawlikowski, all of which is sure to set discriminating viewers swooning.” – Leslie Felperin, The Hollywood Reporter

screenings.title: Rate It X
screenings.description: First released in 1985, RATE IT X stunned audiences and critics alike with its unflinching look at how sexism and sexual exploitation are embedded in American media and culture. Directors Lucy Winer and Paula de Koenigsberg traveled across the United States interviewing men who profited from—and helped perpetuate—stereotyped and sexualized images of women. Advertising executives describe how sex is used to sell product. Hustler magazine’s creator of the notorious “Chester the Molester” cartoon proudly displays drawings depicting a predatory adult man entrapping young girls. A fundamentalist minister tells us that Adam shirked his responsibility by allowing Eve to lead. The flamboyant producer of a popular cable show roams the streets of New York City in a silver lamé jumpsuit, video camera in hand, asking young women, “Would you like to flex into a hallway and pose nude?”

screenings.title: Once Upon A Time In The West
screenings.description: "Along with dream team collaborators Leone and Bernardo Bertolucci, Dario Argento is credited with the story for this epic oater, a sort of link between the established Spaghetti Western and the rising giallo, both genres defined by their elaborate and sometimes insanely involved set pieces. Honest Henry Fonda goes bad—very bad—as a railroad baron’s hired gun, facing off against Bronson’s lethal loner Harmonica, in the soaring, musically composed movie that really earns the label of “horse opera.”

screenings.title: Fjord
screenings.description: From two⁠-⁠time Palme d’Or winner Cristian Mungiu, a Norwegian woman and her devout Romanian husband relocate with their five children to a remote, close⁠-⁠knit, coastal town. Their teenage children form a fast bond with a neighboring family as unease begins to simmer around their rigid beliefs. When allegations of abuse emerge, they are forced to confront a system of judgment that blurs the line between concern and prejudice. In Norwegian, English, Romanian and Swedish with English subtitles.

But when Irwin witnesses something he wasn’t meant to see at the Gowanus Canal, the brothers find themselves pulled into a dangerous confrontation with the newly emerging Russian mafia. As the threat of violence escalates, Irwin’s wife Hester (Scarlett Johansson) sounds the alarm, Irwin desperately tries to protect his family, and Gary is forced to make an impossible choice to save those he loves.

screenings.title: Josephine
screenings.description: JOSEPHINE follows the psychological fallout after eight-year-old Josephine (Mason Reeves) witnesses a brutal crime in Golden Gate Park. As she acts out, her parents (Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan) struggle with helping their daughter cope, while facing the moral responsibility of demanding justice in a world that’s lost its innocence.

screenings.title: Club Kid
screenings.description: A hard-partying NYC club promoter discovers he has a 10-year-old son that he never knew about.

screenings.title: Wild Horse Nine
screenings.description: Shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup, CIA agents Chris (John Malkovich) and Lee (Sam Rockwell) are dispatched from Santiago to Easter island by their bureau chief, MJ (Steve Buscemi). Amongst the Island's iconic statues, and as the longtime partners wrestle with their dark pasts and present conspiracies, Chris's newfound bond with a pair of rebellious students (Mariana di Girolamo and Ailín Salas) threatens to send everyone’s trip to this remote paradise sideways.

screenings.title: The History of Concrete
screenings.description: Following the finale of his TV show, filmmaker John Wilson searches for a new creative outlet. After attending a workshop on how to write and sell a Hallmark movie, he attempts to apply the same formula to a documentary about concrete.

screenings.title: Paper Tiger
screenings.description: James Gray’s latest drama follows two brothers whose bond is threatened by a dangerous scheme.

screenings.title: The Manchurian Candidate
screenings.description: The 1960 U-2 incident, and rumors of the brainwashing of downed Air Force pilot Francis Gary Powers by Soviet captors, were fresh in the imagination when Frankenheimer’s taut political suspenser hit screens, featuring Laurence Harvey as Raymond Shaw, a Korean War vet returned stateside with decorations after going MIA—unbeknownst to himself and the wider world, a sleeper agent programmed to do the bidding of the Commies—and Frank Sinatra the Army Intelligence officer who suspects all might not be right with Sgt. Shaw. “One of the strangest and most mercurial movies ever made in Hollywood… Conceivably the only commercial American film that deserves to be linked with the French New Wave, full of visual and verbal wit that recalls Orson Welles… A powerful experience, alternately corrosive with dark parodic humor, suspenseful, moving, and terrifying.” —Jonathan Rosenbaum, The Chicago Reader

screenings.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
screenings.description: “One of the greatest cinematic works of creative nonfiction that I've ever seen.” – Richard Brody, The New Yorker CRITIC’S PICK. “A house party for the ages... A blissout and one of the events of this cinematic season... A deeply personal, collectively produced oral history of a specific moment of time as it was lived—and held in memory—by specific individuals. The past comes vibrantly alive in these rooms, but always circles back to the present and often points to the future... One of the sustaining pleasures of this wonderful, spirit-lifting movie is that—even with many of its contributors now gone—it feels excitingly alive.” – Manohla Dargis, The New York Times “A MASTERPIECE... A truly monumental work of art.” – Bilge Ebiri, New York Magazine “The stuff of legend... Feels like a miracle.” – Robert Daniels, RogerEbert.com “An atmospheric, electrifying documentary, and a moving testament to the importance of remembering.” – Shirley Li, The Atlantic “An intergenerational feat... A documentary brimming with the wise, the thought-provoking and the deeply entertaining... [A] glimmering gift... with something that resembles a calling forth of the ancestors... A vivid and layered time capsule... Turns viewers into time travelers but also invited guests, rightly grateful to be in the room. For some of us, this film might evoke the wonder of a great-grandchild listening in on grown-up reminiscences. Nodding at the substance. Smiling at the style.” – Lisa Kennedy, Variety “[A] rich doc crafted from gorgeously restored footage. A triumph of DIY filmmaking and an act of cinematic resistance.” – Jourdain Searles, The Hollywood Reporter “A masterpiece.” – David Fear, Rolling Stone “Not only the biggest surprise of this year’s Sundance, but a revelation.” – Chris O’Falt, IndieWire

screenings.title: Queen at Sea
screenings.description: Amanda (Academy Award winner Juliette Binoche, The English Patient, The Taste of Things) and her stepfather Martin (Academy Award nominee Tom Courtenay, Doctor Zhivago, 45 Years) struggle with a moral issue that divides them. Has Amanda’s mother Leslie (Anna Calder-Marshall) who is suffering from advanced dementia, lost the ability to make critical decisions in her own best interests? And, if so, who is responsible – a spouse, a child, an institution – for making such a determination? As Amanda and Martin are forced to make increasingly difficult choices, the repercussions spiral out of their control.

screenings.title: Elsinore
screenings.description: Andrew Scott (Sherlock) stars as Ian Charleson in a story of courage, art, and mortality.

screenings.title: Elsinore
screenings.description: The deeply emotional and inspirational true story of Ian Charleson, a gifted actor whose greatest challenge becomes his greatest triumph. Facing his own mortality with unflinching honesty, wit, and grace, Charleson delivers a courageous performance that becomes a source of healing and inspiration for those around him.

screenings.title: Bitter Christmas
screenings.description: BITTER CHRISTMAS tells two alternating stories, one starring Elsa, an advertising director, in 2004, during a long weekend in December. The second takes place in 2026 and stars Raúl, a screenwriter and director who is writing a script that we soon discover is the story of Elsa, her boyfriend Bonifacio, and her friends Patricia and Natalia. Mixed with fiction, Elsa is, in a way, Raúl's alter ego, who, like him, resorts to autofiction as a solution to a long period of creative drought. He looks inside himself, and he can't help but also look at the people who make up his most intimate universe: his partner and his assistant.

screenings.title: Paper Tiger
screenings.description: In James Gray’s deeply felt and intense drama, two brothers become entangled in a scheme that turns out to be too good to be true. As they try to navigate their way through the dangerous world of the Russian mafia, family bonds begin to fray with life-altering consequences.

screenings.title: Barbara Forever + Q&A
screenings.description: BARBARA FOREVER is an expansive, immersive exploration of the life, work, and ongoing cultural impact of filmmaker Barbara Hammer – a pioneering artist who lived boldly, created urgently, and transformed cinema through her singular vision. Her films were an extension of herself: sensual, experimental, and unapologetically lesbian, rooted in a profound desire for connection and an insistence on telling her own story. Driven by her canon of over eighty films, a vast collection of unreleased archival materials, and extensive audio interviews, Brydie O’Connor’s portrait allows for Hammer’s voice and images to shine through, becoming both a tribute and an extension of her legacy.

screenings.title: 14th
screenings.description: Written in the wreckage of the Civil War, the 14th Amendment was meant to codify the promise of freedom and citizenship. Instead, it has become a permanent argument. Oscar nominee DuVernay’s new documentary pulls this fight out of the footnotes and into the present, chronicling a vicious battle that has raged for more than 150 years. Threading deep archival scholarship with today’s headlines, 14TH brings together legal minds, politicians, historians and cultural voices to explore a question America still hasn’t settled: Who gets to belong?

screenings.title: You Can See Everything
screenings.description: Thirty-four days before she’s sent to prison, notorious Silicon Valley founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a skeptical film crew to document her every move. What begins as an intimate portrait of an enigmatic felon becomes a mind-bending three-year journey into the abyss.

screenings.title: Brigadoon
screenings.description: Dir. Vincente Minnelli. 1954, 108 mins. U.S. 35mm. With Gene Kelly, Cyd Charisse, Van Johnson, Elaine Stewart. One of the first Cinemascope, Technicolor musicals, this MGM extravaganza, adapted from the stage by the great Lerner and Loewe, is an enchanting fantasy in which a pair of New Yorkers find themselves in a magical Scottish town called Brigadoon, which only materializes once every hundred years. No inhabitant of the town can cross the border to leave, or else the town will disappear—but a stranger can stay if he falls in love with someone there. Of course, complications ensue when Gene Kelly’s Tommy finds himself pining for the beautiful Fiona (Cyd Charisse). Featuring splendidly beautiful dance sequences and gorgeous set design, Brigadoon is a poignant supernatural romance about the aching ephemerality of existence. screenings.title: La Bola Negra in 35mm
screenings.description: From Cannes-winning directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi — popularly known as Los Javis —LA BOLA NEGRA follows three generations of men across pivotal moments in Spanish history, bound by pain, desire, and love. Carlos (Milo Quifes) longs to belong in a fractured Spain. Sebastián (Guitarricadelafuente) finds connection across enemy lines. And Alberto (Carlos González) uncovers a long-buried family secret — one that finally gives voice to truths the past tried to erase.

screenings.title: Rome, Open City
screenings.description: “A STILL-THRILLING CALL TO CONSCIENCE AND HOPE! Shot with electrifying urgency months after Rome’s liberation… a cinematic landmark [that brought] Italian neorealism to world-wide attention. Born of wartime trauma and a desire for unity in the new Italy that would come, ROME, OPEN CITY has lost little of its power.” – Kristin M. Jones, Wall Street Journal Read the full review. “THE MOST PRECIOUS MOMENT OF FILM HISTORY!” – Martin Scorsese “ROSSELLINI’S NEOREALIST MASTERPIECE... Aldo Fabrizi is compelling as a sympathetic priest, as is Marcello Pagliero as a cool Communist. But towering over all is Anna Magnani, as a pregnant widow, mother and bride-to-be... Plain-spoken, tender and yet indomitable, she provides the film’s central anima.” – Andy Webster, New York Times “Rossellini’s tense, bloody, death-haunted film conjures an authenticity that’s based less on its quasi-documentary style than on a vision that brings ideas to life. It offers a template for a postwar renewal of Italy, as well as Italian cinema.” – Richard Brody, New Yorker “A LEGENDARY CINEMATIC ACHIEVEMENT! Its justly celebrated documentary aesthetic and naturalistic performances, aided by the filmmakers’ budgetary restrictions and the ruinous state of the postwar Italian film industry, help the work achieve moments of devastating, near miraculous beauty.” – Oleg Ivanov, Slant Read the full review. “The fame of Rossellini’s brutal, melodramatic account of the underground resistance to the Nazi occupation rest on its extraordinary immediacy and its rough, documentary look; at its most startling, it seems ‘caught’ rather than staged. Many Americans, used to slick war films, reacted to it as if it actually were caught… The movie gave us a cross-section of a city under terrible stress.” – Pauline Kael “Rossellini’s Neo-Realism masterpiece... It scarcely matters how many times you watch it... The story plays like a gripping thriller: a cat-and-mouse game between Gestapo and resistance cell.” – Cath Clarke, The Guardian “Still a picture of unrivaled immediacy and passion... memorably preserved a place and a time—and taught generations of filmmakers how to preserve theirs.” – Michael Wilmington “ALL ROADS LEAD TO ROME, OPEN CITY.” – Godard

screenings.title: All of a Sudden
screenings.description: Japan’s Official Selection for Best International Feature Film at the 99th Academy Awards® WINNER, BEST ACTRESS (VIRGINIE EFIRA & TAO OKAMOTO), 2026 CANNES FILM FESTIVAL In the latest film by Oscar®-winning director Ryûsuke Hamaguchi (DRIVE MY CAR), Virginie Efira (BENEDETTA) stars as Marie-Lou, the progressive director of a nursing home in the Parisian suburbs. Her life changes when she meets Mari (Tao Okamoto), Japanese playwright. As the two women reckon with the lives they have lived, they find new ways to make sense of the time that remains. Following caregivers as they navigate the tensions between idealism and pragmatism, Hamaguchi crafts a film that rests fully in the present, attentive to the delicate unfolding of thought, feeling, and human connection. Presented with support from The Reginald S. Reinhardt, Ling-Makekau Fund for Asia-Pacific Films 2026 196 MIN. screenings.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
screenings.description: Harry is an old-school hustler. A classic native New Yorker, he moves through life lubricating palms with cash, relying on his wits and connections. But times are changing for Harry. His daily pickpocket take isn’t green bills and wristwatches, it’s credit cards and cell phones. And one unfortunate night, cryptocurrency and a handgun. THE ONLY LIVING PICKPOCKET IN NEW YORK is a nostalgic portrait of a small-time career criminal navigating today's digitally networked world. Writer/Director Noah Segan's modern metropolis is powered by the ephemera of a time gone by, with shoe-leather action brought to radiant life by a terrific cast, led by John Turturro's exceptional turn as Harry.

screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.title: In Waves
screenings.description: Amid the sun-filled surf culture of SoCal, two lovestruck teens face a tragic twist of fate but find strength in friends and the ocean. In French and English with English subtitles.

screenings.title: Blood Brunch
screenings.description: Calling all Bloodeaters, Love Butchers and Neon Maniacs! The lights go down, the screen lights up and every one of your senses is flooded with ghastly terror from beyond the fetid grave. Spend your Sundays drenched in blood and quivering in fear with a mystery movie—as in, we don’t tell you what we’re showing until you see the title on the screen—that is at least 20 years old.

screenings.title: Minotaur
screenings.description: Intrigue, corruption, betrayal, survival: the walls of the maze are closing in. The latest from Oscar® nominated writer-director Andrey Zvyagintsev (Loveless, Leviathan), Cannes Grand Prix winner MINOTAUR is a twist-laden parable for our times. Russia, 2022. Amidst the comfortable trappings of affluence and domesticity, corporate executive Gleb (Dmitriy Mazurov) finds himself under siege on all fronts. At home, he is haunted by suspicions that his increasingly distant wife Galina (Iris Lebedeva) is unfaithful. At work, he contends with a demand from local authorities to draft a quota of employees for the war in Ukraine. Desperate to keep his hands clean, Gleb struggles to reassert control even as the collapse of his carefully ordered life seems fated to accelerate toward violence. A pressure cooker in cinematic form, MINOTAUR uncovers and indicts the heart of societal darkness with searing clarity. Uniting intimately-drawn performances and stark visual power, France’s Best International Feature Film entry to the 99th Academy Awards® is peerless work from an indisputable master.

The film’s sound has been remastered from original English Composite 35mm Mag Film, transferred at 96kHz, plus other original film elements in selected spots as needed. The Picture and Sound restoration was performed by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color, and Warner Bros. Sound.

screenings.title: Dragon Superman
screenings.description: A breakout success that spawned two sequels in rapid succession, Dragon Superman introduced Taiwanese audiences to the titular masked crusader, by day straight-arrow newspaperman San Lin, by night the bane of the chaos-sowing, satin suit-clad, hydrocephalic members of the Cosmos Gang. Fans of the Adam West Batman series, Mario Bava’s Danger: Diabolik, Japanese tokusatsu pictures, and swinging ’60s superheroics in general will find much to enjoy in this vivacious action romp, starring Kuei Chih-pang as the be-scarfed, motorcycle-riding vigilante, who has his hands full protecting a blind chanteuse (Wu Min), a supermarket magnate (Yang Weixi), and a hunk of Incan gold from the ne’er-do-wells.

screenings.title: Fjord
screenings.description: From two⁠-⁠time Palme d’Or winner Cristian Mungiu, a Norwegian woman and her devout Romanian husband relocate with their five children to a remote, close⁠-⁠knit, coastal town. Their teenage children form a fast bond with a neighboring family as unease begins to simmer around their rigid beliefs. When allegations of abuse emerge, they are forced to confront a system of judgment that blurs the line between concern and prejudice. In Norwegian, English, Romanian and Swedish with English subtitles.

screenings.title: Fatherland
screenings.description: ★★★★★ “Another expansive, enriching work from a modern master.” – Phil de Semlyen, Time Out “A perfectly cut jewel of a movie... The power of the movie creeps up on you with its emotional restraint, the beauty of its black-and-white images and the delicacy with which Pawlikowski explores the devastations trembling under the faces of both father and daughter...” – Manohla Dargis, The New York Times “Stunning... an exquisite study of family, identity, and art where future ideals are intertwined with historical remorse.” – Tomris Laffly, Elle “[A] damn-near perfect period piece... Told with exacting restraint yet as layered as the lacquer on an ebony Biedermeier console, this forms a loose triptych with Pawlikowski’s last two features, IDA and COLD WAR, both of which were set at least partly behind the Iron Curtain... It is immaculately performed by Zischler and especially Hüller, grounding the film throughout with an uncanny, expressive stillness. But it is also exquisitely rendered in the same boxy ratio and silvery monochrome lensing Pawlikowski and DP Lukasz Zal (THE ZONE OF INTEREST) deployed on IDA and COLD WAR, and scrupulously detailed down to the ruined buildings, sharply cut suits, surly restaurant service and eclectic selection of jazz, classical and folk tunes chosen by Pawlikowski, all of which is sure to set discriminating viewers swooning.” – Leslie Felperin, The Hollywood Reporter

screenings.title: Arthur
screenings.description: Dir. Steve Gordon. 1981, 97 mins. U.S. 35mm. With Dudley Moore, Liza Minnelli, John Gielgud, Geraldine Fitzgerald, Jill Eikenberry. This madcap New York City farce stars Dudley Moore as an alcoholic playboy man-child who has lived off the millions inherited from his parents and has never had to work a day in his life. Aided in all endeavors public and private by his endlessly sharp-tongued butler Hobson (an Oscar-winning John Gielgud, delivering one incredible one-liner after another), Arthur lives in a cocoon of privilege, until he falls hard for Liza Minnelli’s down-to-earth working-class shoplifter Linda Marolla. What Arthur lacks in sensitivity towards its character’s drinking problem, it more than makes up for in its perfect mix of sweetness and laugh-out-loud hilarity, and Moore and Minnelli make one of the 1980s’ greatest and most unexpected romcom couples. screenings.title: Raise the Red Lantern
screenings.description: China/Hong Kong, 1991 Directed by Zhang Yimou Starring Gong Li, Saifei He, Jingwu Ma, Cuifen Cao In Mandarin with English subtitles Approx. 125 min. Nineteen-year-old Songlian, a promising student whose family has been destroyed by her father’s death, is forced to abandon her studies and marry into wealth, becoming the fourth and newest concubine of the aging, unseen Master Chen. Inside his walled estate, she discovers a household ruled by a merciless ritual: each night, red lanterns are lit outside the chambers of whichever wife the master chooses to visit, granting her privilege and status while the others are cast into cold irrelevance. Songlian is drawn into the orbit of her rivals, each shaped by years of fighting for the same scraps of attention. Determined at first to rise above the games, Songlian is gradually worn down by isolation and humiliation until she strikes back, trading secrets and favors to secure her place in Master Chen’s hierarchy. As petty cruelty turns even more dire, Songlian is forced to confront what these desperate measures will cost her soul. Newly restored, RAISE THE RED LANTERN remains a landmark of Fifth Generation Chinese cinema and 1990s international film. The 4K restoration of RAISE THE RED LANTERN was carried out by the Udine Far East Film Festival on the occasion of its 26th edition. The original image and sound negatives were used under the supervision of Director Zhang Yimou. The vintage positive copy, presented at the 1991 Venice International Film Festival and preserved at the Venice Biennale's Historical Archive of Contemporary Arts, was used for color reference. The restoration was made in 2024 at L'Immagine Ritrovata (Hong Kong – Bologna). Presented with support from The Reginald S. Reinhardt, Ling-Makekau Fund for Asia-Pacific Films and The Ada Katz Fund for Literature in Film A FILM MOVEMENT RELEASE

screenings.title: The Piano
screenings.description: Gale-force winds and interminable lashing rain render colonial New Zealand a nigh uninhabitable mire in Campion’s elemental Antipodean Gothic romance, in which mute Scotswoman Ada and her young daughter (Holly Hunter, Anna Paquin) arrive under the Southern Cross so that Ada can be wed to stiff-backed settler Alisdair Stewart (Sam Neill)—an arranged union that quickly sours when Stewart separates Ada from her lone means of expression, her piano, and Ada drifts into an increasingly compromising and sexualized relationship with neighbor George Baines (Harvey Keitel), an ex-sailor and the instrument’s new owner. With its Palme d’Or win at Cannes, Campion became the first female director to receive that honor—and a shower of Academy Awards still lay ahead.

screenings.title: Germany, Year Zero
screenings.description: GERMANIA, ANNO ZERO Italy/France/Germany, 1948 Directed by Roberto Rossellini Starring Edmund Moeschke, Ernst Pittschau, Ingetraud Hinze Approx. 78 min. 35mm. Following the international acclaim and box office success of ROME, OPEN CITY and PAISAN, Rossellini took the first of many obstreperous swerves that would come to define his career. His next film would be another dispatch from war-torn Europe, with scenes playing out amidst the rubble with unvarnished immediacy, with unfamiliar and nonprofessional actors populating the cast—but this time, the protagonists would not be resistance fighters liberating Italy, but the defeated Germans muddling through their wasteland reich. Financed largely by the French government, GERMANY, YEAR ZERO became an experiment in radical empathy and its limits, casting about for signs of new life in a nation of crooks, unrepentant Nazis, and pederasts. The only innocent soul is twelve-year-old protagonist Edmund, who cannot qualify for a work permit, but must somehow earn a living to support his household. Even the child recognizes that he has no role models in this world: his brother is a mopey ex-soldier who refuses to register for a ration card, his father is an invalid who muses he’d be better off dead, his neighbors are coarse and severe, his friends are common swindlers, and his former school teacher still preaches that the strong must snuff out the weak. Unsentimental in the extreme and devoid of any comic relief, GERMANY YEAR ZERO plays like a seance for souls who have yet to recognize themselves as the walking dead. 35mm print courtesy Cinecittà.

Fiction makes way for what Frederick Wiseman once dubbed, in a different context, reality-fiction: the kids eventually forget they’re acting and bring their own lives into the film. screenings.title: Dov’è La Libertà?
screenings.description: Italy, 1954 Directed by Roberto Rossellini Starring Totò, Vera Molnar, Nyta Dover Approx. 93 min. Incarcerated for twenty-two years after committing a crime of passion, Salvatore Lojacono (Totò) wins parole and returns to a Rome that he scarcely recognizes—and ultimately decides that prison is preferable. Salvatore learns the hard way that business, romance, and family are all elaborate rackets; even the most sympathetic victim he encounters is just on the hunt for a tax swap. His disenchantment is recounted in flashback, as he begs a judge to lock him back up. (The courtroom scenes were, in fact, shot later by Mario Monicelli, after Rossellini abandoned the project in mid-production, and effectively bridged the patchwork of episodes left behind.) The popular Neapolitan comedian Totò gets plenty of opportunities to mug, but also flexes his dramatic muscles as a man who trusts too tenderly. The scenario was inspired by Chaplin’s MODERN TIMES, but the moral vision is closer to MONSIEUR VERDOUX, another comedy born of the recognition that post-war society has been stripped of sentimental illusions and re-organized under principles of ruthless capitalism indistinguishable from the barbarism it displaced. “It stupefied me with its cruelty and bitterness,” wrote Pierre Kast in Cahiers du Cinema, long a bastion of Rossellini apologetics. “It’s a parable of the purest Swiftian type, unpitying and almost intolerable.” Courtesy Rialto Pictures.

Nineteen-year-old Songlian, a promising student whose family has been destroyed by her father’s death, is forced to abandon her studies and marry into wealth, becoming the fourth and newest concubine of the aging, unseen Master Chen. Inside his walled estate, she discovers a household ruled by a merciless ritual: each night, red lanterns are lit outside the chambers of whichever wife the master chooses to visit, granting her privilege and status while the others are cast into cold irrelevance. Songlian is drawn into the orbit of her rivals, each shaped by years of fighting for the same scraps of attention. Determined at first to rise above the games, Songlian is gradually worn down by isolation and humiliation until she strikes back, trading secrets and favors to secure her place in Master Chen’s hierarchy. As petty cruelty turns even more dire, Songlian is forced to confront what these desperate measures will cost her soul. Newly restored, RAISE THE RED LANTERN remains a landmark of Fifth Generation Chinese cinema and 1990s international film. The 4K restoration of RAISE THE RED LANTERN was carried out by the Udine Far East Film Festival on the occasion of its 26th edition. The original image and sound negatives were used under the supervision of Director Zhang Yimou. The vintage positive copy, presented at the 1991 Venice International Film Festival and preserved at the Venice Biennale's Historical Archive of Contemporary Arts, was used for color reference. The restoration was made in 2024 at L'Immagine Ritrovata (Hong Kong – Bologna). Presented with support from The Reginald S. What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. screenings.title: General Della Rovere
screenings.description: IL GENERALE DELLA ROVERE Italy/France, 1959 Directed by Roberto Rossellini Starring Vittorio De Sica, Hannes Messemer, Sandra Milo, Anne Vernon Approx. 132 min. 35mm. Based on the true story of Italian cavalry officer Giovanni Bertone during World War II, GENERAL DELLA ROVERE recounts the unexpected moral evolution of Emanuele Bardone (Vittorio de Sica), an ingratiating swindler with a talent for improvising novel solutions to the dilemmas he has sprung on himself. Alas, even when Bardone wins, he feels compelled to double-down and gamble away his momentary advantage. He has a talent for extracting favors from the Nazi officers in Genoa, and when the law catches up to Bardone, he’s offered a bargain: go to prison and imitate the Italian general Della Rovere, in hopes of penetrating his resistance network. De Sica’s big and boisterous performance anchors the film, and renders this somber story of ethical compromise into an improbable crowdpleaser. Rossellini considered GENERAL DELLA ROVERE an embarrassing capitulation, a work-for-hire to demonstrate that he could, under duress, follow a script and a schedule. Shot quickly on studio sets with some undisguised rear projection footage, GENERAL DELLA ROVERE went on to win the Golden Lion at the Venice Film Festival and revitalize Rossellini’s career after a decade of box office setbacks. Like Bardone, Rossellini always had another trick up his sleeve. 35mm print courtesy Cinecittà. Presented with support from The Ada Katz Fund for Literature in Film

screenings.title: Salò, or the 120 Days of Sodom
screenings.description: Pasolini’s final film remains one of the most shocking ever made. Set during a waning fascist Italy’s dark days amidst World War II, Salò updates the writings of Marquis de Sade to create a repugnant tale of four wealthy libertines who kidnap a group of teenage boys and girls and enact horrific humiliations and violence upon them. A formally and conceptually brilliant, if relentlessly nauseating, portrayal of man’s most debased instincts and the capitalist systems that allow them to thrive. Per Pasolini, “The most sincere thing I could do at that moment was to make a film about a mode of sexuality whose joyousness is a compensation for repression—a phenomenon that was about to come to an end, forever.”

screenings.title: Minotaur

The latest from Oscar® nominated writer-director Andrey Zvyagintsev (Loveless, Leviathan), Cannes Grand Prix winner MINOTAUR is a twist-laden parable for our times. Russia, 2022. Amidst the comfortable trappings of affluence and domesticity, corporate executive Gleb (Dmitriy Mazurov) finds himself under siege on all fronts. At home, he is haunted by suspicions that his increasingly distant wife Galina (Iris Lebedeva) is unfaithful. At work, he contends with a demand from local authorities to draft a quota of employees for the war in Ukraine. Desperate to keep his hands clean, Gleb struggles to reassert control even as the collapse of his carefully ordered life seems fated to accelerate toward violence. A pressure cooker in cinematic form, MINOTAUR uncovers and indicts the heart of societal darkness with searing clarity. Uniting intimately-drawn performances and stark visual power, France’s Best International Feature Film entry to the 99th Academy Awards® is peerless work from an indisputable master.

screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

When her own daughter’s future becomes entangled with the past, Vénéranda is forced to find her own words at last.

screenings.description: PAISÀ Italy, 1946 Directed by Roberto Rossellini Starring Carmela Sazio, Robert Van Loon, Dots Johnson Approx. 126 min. 35mm. The story of Italy’s liberation, told in six episodes, traveling from the first Allied landing in Sicily to the battle of the Po Delta, PAISAN demonstrated that OPEN CITY had been no fluke. Conceived on a vaster scale, with a considerably higher budget, and international distribution from MGM, PAISAN is a national epic that still startles for its immediacy, its technical mastery, its unpredictable rhythms. Scenes of unbearable suspense on the streets of Florence alternate with lighter fare, such as the doctrinal scuffles between Italian monks and American chaplains in Romagna. Stitched together like a newsreel (and skillfully edited to blend in stock footage and suggest off-screen pyrotechnics with creative sound effects), PAISAN became a worldwide sensation, an intellectual action film that pictured recent history with an unprecedented heft and scope. The film became a lodestar for filmmakers from Gillo Pontecorvo to Martin Scorsese, with the latter remarking, “The result... is still startling: it’s like seeing reality itself unfolding before your eyes.” 35mm print courtesy Cinecittà.

screenings.description: First released in 1985, RATE IT X stunned audiences and critics alike with its unflinching look at how sexism and sexual exploitation are embedded in American media and culture. Directors Lucy Winer and Paula de Koenigsberg traveled across the United States interviewing men who profited from—and helped perpetuate—stereotyped and sexualized images of women. Advertising executives describe how sex is used to sell product. Hustler magazine’s creator of the notorious “Chester the Molester” cartoon proudly displays drawings depicting a predatory adult man entrapping young girls. A fundamentalist minister tells us that Adam shirked his responsibility by allowing Eve to lead. The flamboyant producer of a popular cable show roams the streets of New York City in a silver lamé jumpsuit, video camera in hand, asking young women, “Would you like to flex into a hallway and pose nude?”

As she acts out, her parents (Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan) struggle with helping their daughter cope, while facing the moral responsibility of demanding justice in a world that’s lost its innocence.

screenings.title: Wild Horse Nine

screenings.description: Following the finale of his TV show, filmmaker John Wilson searches for a new creative outlet. After attending a workshop on how to write and sell a Hallmark movie, he attempts to apply the same formula to a documentary about concrete.

screenings.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
screenings.description: “One of the greatest cinematic works of creative nonfiction that I've ever seen.” – Richard Brody, The New Yorker CRITIC’S PICK. “A house party for the ages... A blissout and one of the events of this cinematic season... A deeply personal, collectively produced oral history of a specific moment of time as it was lived—and held in memory—by specific individuals. The past comes vibrantly alive in these rooms, but always circles back to the present and often points to the future... One of the sustaining pleasures of this wonderful, spirit-lifting movie is that—even with many of its contributors now gone—it feels excitingly alive.” – Manohla Dargis, The New York Times “A MASTERPIECE... A truly monumental work of art.” – Bilge Ebiri, New York Magazine “The stuff of legend... Feels like a miracle.” – Robert Daniels, RogerEbert.com “An atmospheric, electrifying documentary, and a moving testament to the importance of remembering.” – Shirley Li, The Atlantic “An intergenerational feat... A documentary brimming with the wise, the thought-provoking and the deeply entertaining... [A] glimmering gift... with something that resembles a calling forth of the ancestors... A vivid and layered time capsule... Turns viewers into time travelers but also invited guests, rightly grateful to be in the room. For some of us, this film might evoke the wonder of a great-grandchild listening in on grown-up reminiscences. Nodding at the substance. Smiling at the style.” – Lisa Kennedy, Variety “[A] rich doc crafted from gorgeously restored footage. A triumph of DIY filmmaking and an act of cinematic resistance.” – Jourdain Searles, The Hollywood Reporter “A masterpiece.” – David Fear, Rolling Stone “Not only the biggest surprise of this year’s Sundance, but a revelation.” – Chris O’Falt, IndieWire

screenings.title: Queen at Sea
screenings.description: Amanda (Academy Award winner Juliette Binoche, The English Patient, The Taste of Things) and her stepfather Martin (Academy Award nominee Tom Courtenay, Doctor Zhivago, 45 Years) struggle with a moral issue that divides them. Has Amanda’s mother Leslie (Anna Calder-Marshall) who is suffering from advanced dementia, lost the ability to make critical decisions in her own best interests? And, if so, who is responsible – a spouse, a child, an institution – for making such a determination? As Amanda and Martin are forced to make increasingly difficult choices, the repercussions spiral out of their control.

screenings.title: Elsinore

Facing his own mortality with unflinching honesty, wit, and grace, Charleson delivers a courageous performance that becomes a source of healing and inspiration for those around him.

screenings.title: Bitter Christmas
screenings.description: BITTER CHRISTMAS tells two alternating stories, one starring Elsa, an advertising director, in 2004, during a long weekend in December. The second takes place in 2026 and stars Raúl, a screenwriter and director who is writing a script that we soon discover is the story of Elsa, her boyfriend Bonifacio, and her friends Patricia and Natalia. Mixed with fiction, Elsa is, in a way, Raúl's alter ego, who, like him, resorts to autofiction as a solution to a long period of creative drought. He looks inside himself, and he can't help but also look at the people who make up his most intimate universe: his partner and his assistant.

screenings.title: 14th
screenings.description: Written in the wreckage of the Civil War, the 14th Amendment was meant to codify the promise of freedom and citizenship. Instead, it has become a permanent argument. Oscar nominee DuVernay’s new documentary pulls this fight out of the footnotes and into the present, chronicling a vicious battle that has raged for more than 150 years. Threading deep archival scholarship with today’s headlines, 14TH brings together legal minds, politicians, historians and cultural voices to explore a question America still hasn’t settled: Who gets to belong?

screenings.title: Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall in 35mm
screenings.description: Cameron Winter, in December 2025, after a months-long sold-out tour with his band Geese, returned to New York to play a single show at Carnegie Hall. This is the movie. Directed and shot on 35mm and 16mm by Oscar-winning filmmaker Paul Thomas Anderson (One Battle After Another), the crew includes filmmaker and actor Benny Safdie (The Smashing Machine) and music producer Ariel Rechtshaid (Grammy winner for albums with Vampire Weekend and Adele). GQ praised Cameron Winter’s show at Carnegie Hall as “staggeringly good,” and Nick Cave said he has a "a glorious, emotive voice with brilliant, blistering words, a racked and wondrous thing.” Winter’s solo album Heavy Metal was named one of the best of the year by Pitchfork, Rolling Stone, Paste and Mojo and Geese’s last record Getting Killed was named the best album of 2025 by The New Yorker, NME, and Stereogum.

Her life changes when she meets Mari (Tao Okamoto), Japanese playwright. As the two women reckon with the lives they have lived, they find new ways to make sense of the time that remains. Following caregivers as they navigate the tensions between idealism and pragmatism, Hamaguchi crafts a film that rests fully in the present, attentive to the delicate unfolding of thought, feeling, and human connection. screenings.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
screenings.description: Harry is an old-school hustler. A classic native New Yorker, he moves through life lubricating palms with cash, relying on his wits and connections. But times are changing for Harry. His daily pickpocket take isn’t green bills and wristwatches, it’s credit cards and cell phones. And one unfortunate night, cryptocurrency and a handgun. THE ONLY LIVING PICKPOCKET IN NEW YORK is a nostalgic portrait of a small-time career criminal navigating today's digitally networked world. Writer/Director Noah Segan's modern metropolis is powered by the ephemera of a time gone by, with shoe-leather action brought to radiant life by a terrific cast, led by John Turturro's exceptional turn as Harry.

screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.title: In Waves
screenings.description: Amid the sun-filled surf culture of SoCal, two lovestruck teens face a tragic twist of fate but find strength in friends and the ocean. In French and English with English subtitles.

screenings.title: General Della Rovere
screenings.description: IL GENERALE DELLA ROVERE Italy/France, 1959 Directed by Roberto Rossellini Starring Vittorio De Sica, Hannes Messemer, Sandra Milo, Anne Vernon Approx. 132 min. 35mm. Based on the true story of Italian cavalry officer Giovanni Bertone during World War II, GENERAL DELLA ROVERE recounts the unexpected moral evolution of Emanuele Bardone (Vittorio de Sica), an ingratiating swindler with a talent for improvising novel solutions to the dilemmas he has sprung on himself. Alas, even when Bardone wins, he feels compelled to double-down and gamble away his momentary advantage. He has a talent for extracting favors from the Nazi officers in Genoa, and when the law catches up to Bardone, he’s offered a bargain: go to prison and imitate the Italian general Della Rovere, in hopes of penetrating his resistance network. De Sica’s big and boisterous performance anchors the film, and renders this somber story of ethical compromise into an improbable crowdpleaser. Rossellini considered GENERAL DELLA ROVERE an embarrassing capitulation, a work-for-hire to demonstrate that he could, under duress, follow a script and a schedule. Shot quickly on studio sets with some undisguised rear projection footage, GENERAL DELLA ROVERE went on to win the Golden Lion at the Venice Film Festival and revitalize Rossellini’s career after a decade of box office setbacks. Like Bardone, Rossellini always had another trick up his sleeve. 35mm print courtesy Cinecittà. Presented with support from The Ada Katz Fund for Literature in Film

screenings.title: Minotaur
screenings.description: Intrigue, corruption, betrayal, survival: the walls of the maze are closing in. The latest from Oscar® nominated writer-director Andrey Zvyagintsev (Loveless, Leviathan), Cannes Grand Prix winner MINOTAUR is a twist-laden parable for our times. Russia, 2022. Amidst the comfortable trappings of affluence and domesticity, corporate executive Gleb (Dmitriy Mazurov) finds himself under siege on all fronts. At home, he is haunted by suspicions that his increasingly distant wife Galina (Iris Lebedeva) is unfaithful. At work, he contends with a demand from local authorities to draft a quota of employees for the war in Ukraine. Desperate to keep his hands clean, Gleb struggles to reassert control even as the collapse of his carefully ordered life seems fated to accelerate toward violence. A pressure cooker in cinematic form, MINOTAUR uncovers and indicts the heart of societal darkness with searing clarity. Uniting intimately-drawn performances and stark visual power, France’s Best International Feature Film entry to the 99th Academy Awards® is peerless work from an indisputable master.

screenings.title: Raise the Red Lantern
screenings.description: China/Hong Kong, 1991 Directed by Zhang Yimou Starring Gong Li, Saifei He, Jingwu Ma, Cuifen Cao In Mandarin with English subtitles Approx. 125 min. Nineteen-year-old Songlian, a promising student whose family has been destroyed by her father’s death, is forced to abandon her studies and marry into wealth, becoming the fourth and newest concubine of the aging, unseen Master Chen. Inside his walled estate, she discovers a household ruled by a merciless ritual: each night, red lanterns are lit outside the chambers of whichever wife the master chooses to visit, granting her privilege and status while the others are cast into cold irrelevance. Songlian is drawn into the orbit of her rivals, each shaped by years of fighting for the same scraps of attention. Determined at first to rise above the games, Songlian is gradually worn down by isolation and humiliation until she strikes back, trading secrets and favors to secure her place in Master Chen’s hierarchy. As petty cruelty turns even more dire, Songlian is forced to confront what these desperate measures will cost her soul. Newly restored, RAISE THE RED LANTERN remains a landmark of Fifth Generation Chinese cinema and 1990s international film. The 4K restoration of RAISE THE RED LANTERN was carried out by the Udine Far East Film Festival on the occasion of its 26th edition. The original image and sound negatives were used under the supervision of Director Zhang Yimou. The vintage positive copy, presented at the 1991 Venice International Film Festival and preserved at the Venice Biennale's Historical Archive of Contemporary Arts, was used for color reference. The restoration was made in 2024 at L'Immagine Ritrovata (Hong Kong – Bologna). Presented with support from The Reginald S. screenings.title: Rome, Open City
screenings.description: “A STILL-THRILLING CALL TO CONSCIENCE AND HOPE! Shot with electrifying urgency months after Rome’s liberation… a cinematic landmark [that brought] Italian neorealism to world-wide attention. Born of wartime trauma and a desire for unity in the new Italy that would come, ROME, OPEN CITY has lost little of its power.” – Kristin M. Jones, Wall Street Journal Read the full review. “THE MOST PRECIOUS MOMENT OF FILM HISTORY!” – Martin Scorsese “ROSSELLINI’S NEOREALIST MASTERPIECE... Aldo Fabrizi is compelling as a sympathetic priest, as is Marcello Pagliero as a cool Communist. But towering over all is Anna Magnani, as a pregnant widow, mother and bride-to-be... Plain-spoken, tender and yet indomitable, she provides the film’s central anima.” – Andy Webster, New York Times “Rossellini’s tense, bloody, death-haunted film conjures an authenticity that’s based less on its quasi-documentary style than on a vision that brings ideas to life. It offers a template for a postwar renewal of Italy, as well as Italian cinema.” – Richard Brody, New Yorker “A LEGENDARY CINEMATIC ACHIEVEMENT! Its justly celebrated documentary aesthetic and naturalistic performances, aided by the filmmakers’ budgetary restrictions and the ruinous state of the postwar Italian film industry, help the work achieve moments of devastating, near miraculous beauty.” – Oleg Ivanov, Slant Read the full review. “The fame of Rossellini’s brutal, melodramatic account of the underground resistance to the Nazi occupation rest on its extraordinary immediacy and its rough, documentary look; at its most startling, it seems ‘caught’ rather than staged. Many Americans, used to slick war films, reacted to it as if it actually were caught… The movie gave us a cross-section of a city under terrible stress.” – Pauline Kael “Rossellini’s Neo-Realism masterpiece... It scarcely matters how many times you watch it... The story plays like a gripping thriller: a cat-and-mouse game between Gestapo and resistance cell.” – Cath Clarke, The Guardian “Still a picture of unrivaled immediacy and passion... memorably preserved a place and a time—and taught generations of filmmakers how to preserve theirs.” – Michael Wilmington “ALL ROADS LEAD TO ROME, OPEN CITY.” – Godard

screenings.title: Scenes from the Divide
screenings.description: In the lead-up to Zohran Mamdani’s election as mayor of New York City, many of the city’s Jewish population found themselves at odds over the candidate’s positions on Palestine and Israel. By inviting viewers into the homes of New Yorkers on both sides of the campaign, DOC NYC alumna Alison Klayman (Jagged; Ai Weiwei: Never Sorry) reveals a fierce battle among American Jews over identity, history, and responsibility. SCENES FROM THE DIVIDE explores a community in generational upheaval.

screenings.description: China/Hong Kong, 1991 Directed by Zhang Yimou Starring Gong Li, Saifei He, Jingwu Ma, Cuifen Cao In Mandarin with English subtitles Approx. 125 min. Nineteen-year-old Songlian, a promising student whose family has been destroyed by her father’s death, is forced to abandon her studies and marry into wealth, becoming the fourth and newest concubine of the aging, unseen Master Chen. Inside his walled estate, she discovers a household ruled by a merciless ritual: each night, red lanterns are lit outside the chambers of whichever wife the master chooses to visit, granting her privilege and status while the others are cast into cold irrelevance. Songlian is drawn into the orbit of her rivals, each shaped by years of fighting for the same scraps of attention. Determined at first to rise above the games, Songlian is gradually worn down by isolation and humiliation until she strikes back, trading secrets and favors to secure her place in Master Chen’s hierarchy. As petty cruelty turns even more dire, Songlian is forced to confront what these desperate measures will cost her soul. Newly restored, RAISE THE RED LANTERN remains a landmark of Fifth Generation Chinese cinema and 1990s international film. The 4K restoration of RAISE THE RED LANTERN was carried out by the Udine Far East Film Festival on the occasion of its 26th edition. The original image and sound negatives were used under the supervision of Director Zhang Yimou. The vintage positive copy, presented at the 1991 Venice International Film Festival and preserved at the Venice Biennale's Historical Archive of Contemporary Arts, was used for color reference. The restoration was made in 2024 at L'Immagine Ritrovata (Hong Kong – Bologna). Presented with support from The Reginald S. screenings.title: 14th (Open Captioning)

Threading deep archival scholarship with today’s headlines, 14TH brings together legal minds, politicians, historians and cultural voices to explore a question America still hasn’t settled: Who gets to belong?

screenings.title: The Scout + Q&A

Over a day filled with these encounters, Sofia witnesses moments of curiosity, vulnerability, and quiet tension until her work takes a sudden, personal turn. Drawing from her own experience as a location scout, writer-director Paula González-Nasser captures the poetry and costs of being a young creative. Her celebrated directorial debut The Scout crafts a contemplative exploration of urban disconnection, following one woman’s journey through other people’s worlds as she struggles to find her own.

screenings.title: The Mad Songs of Fernanda Hussein
screenings.description: Boston-based filmmaker and former Harvard Film Archive curator John Gianvito had made a few films before the 20th century became the 21st, but he would wind up emerging as one of the definitive filmmakers of the current century during its first decade. His six years of work on Gulf War I cri de cœur The Mad Songs of Fernanda Hussein wound up serving as one of the definitive commentaries on the upcoming century when it premiered in 2001. Mad Songs served as a work of inadvertent commentary on the bloodlust spurred by the Twin Tower attacks, and the Gulf War II that was going to come about as a result. It was also a work of intensely personal cinephilia-inspired curation: Griffith- and Wyler-adjacent structuring of multiple war-at-home storylines was melded with archival footage and performance documentary, resulting in a bold and sprawling hybrid work. Despite fierce advocacy from notable champions in Chantal Akerman, Peter Watkins, Jonathan Rosenbaum, and Dennis Lim, it was not an easy film to see in 2001 and it has not gotten much easier since. He’d take another six years to make his next film, this time decidedly aimed at the domestic. Profit Motive and the Whispering Wind (2007) was a film whose more minimalist scale and running time didn’t reduce its power. Its simultaneously rousing and despairing analysis, courtesy of Howard Zinn, marked a turn towards a more domestic issue: how America eats its rabble rousers but leaves a tribute to them later. The groundwork laid by the champions of Mad Songs resulted in Profit Motive finding more of an audience, and it subsequently being named the Best Experimental Film of 2007 by the National Society of Film Critics.

screenings.title: Socrates
screenings.description: Beginning in the mid-’60s and ending with his death in 1977, Rossellini committed himself to producing a series of films, telefilms, and serial works that would together constitute a narrative of human progress and the history of ideas from aleolithic to present times. Socrates, initiating a tetralogy of works on epoch-defining thinkers, sets its scene in an Athens humbled by Sparta and increasingly irritated by the prickly, prodding philosopher in their midst, finally determined to silence him. Using out-of-vogue in-camera effects to transform an ancient Spanish village into Athens, probing scenes with his customized, remote-controlled Pancinor zoom, and employing a dirge-like electronic score by Mario Nascimbene, Rossellini gives us a singular vision of antiquity, one that’s downright avant-garde.

screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.title: Europa '51
screenings.description: Italy, 1952 Directed by Roberto Rossellini Starring Ingrid Bergman, Alexander Knox, Giulietta Masina, Ettore Gianini Approx. 110 min. Shortly after completing THE FLOWERS OF ST. FRANCIS, Rossellini seized upon a hypothetical: if Francis himself appeared in Europe today and preached his humble doctrine, he would be promptly thrown in an insane asylum. Augmented by ideas derived from Simone Weil and Herbert Marcuse, Rossellini’s thought experiment grew and grew until it became EUROPA ’51, a sweeping state-of-the-continent address aimed at the complacency of post-war society. Luckily, Rossellini retained the services of his wife to put a box office spin on this dense rumination. (It would become, ironically, the only one of their pictures together to do any business in Italy.) Irene Gerard (Ingrid Bergman) is a socialite who’s more focused on throwing a good dinner party than attending to the needs of her young son. When the boy kills himself, Irene’s world is shattered: what could drive a child to so thoroughly reject life, and what can she make of the life that remains? Inspired by her cousin’s commitment to the class struggle, Irene begins devoting her time to Rome’s downtrodden. After all, the sick, the dying, and the poor need her more than her husband (Alexander Knox) ever could, do they not? Is Bergman preaching Communist revolution, Christian neighborliness, or some obscure, hyper-personal fusion of the two? Disarmingly literal and unspeakably sincere in its spiritual crusade, EUROPA ‘51 remains the most mysterious of Bergman and Rossellini’s collaborations. Courtesy Janus Films.

screenings.title: Fatherland
screenings.description: ★★★★★ “Another expansive, enriching work from a modern master.” – Phil de Semlyen, Time Out “A perfectly cut jewel of a movie... The power of the movie creeps up on you with its emotional restraint, the beauty of its black-and-white images and the delicacy with which Pawlikowski explores the devastations trembling under the faces of both father and daughter...” – Manohla Dargis, The New York Times “Stunning... an exquisite study of family, identity, and art where future ideals are intertwined with historical remorse.” – Tomris Laffly, Elle “[A] damn-near perfect period piece... Told with exacting restraint yet as layered as the lacquer on an ebony Biedermeier console, this forms a loose triptych with Pawlikowski’s last two features, IDA and COLD WAR, both of which were set at least partly behind the Iron Curtain... It is immaculately performed by Zischler and especially Hüller, grounding the film throughout with an uncanny, expressive stillness. But it is also exquisitely rendered in the same boxy ratio and silvery monochrome lensing Pawlikowski and DP Lukasz Zal (THE ZONE OF INTEREST) deployed on IDA and COLD WAR, and scrupulously detailed down to the ruined buildings, sharply cut suits, surly restaurant service and eclectic selection of jazz, classical and folk tunes chosen by Pawlikowski, all of which is sure to set discriminating viewers swooning.” – Leslie Felperin, The Hollywood Reporter
